# `scatter_on_points`
Generates a points object who points are distributed in various ways around a set of input points.  This is useful for "clustering" scattered points as well as creating different distributions.  As well as a point object output, the compound outputs the points positions, normals, colours and distance to the local point center (originating point) as nested arrays (scatter per input point).  This allows for fine control of instancing on output.

## Inputs

### `points_in`
The point vectors that you wish to use as the center of your scatters.

### `density_weights`
Weights per point of the input geometry to control the distribution of generated points.
* A weight of 0 or less means that no points are generated nearby.
* A weight in the range 0—1 means that fewer than the normal number of points are generated nearby.
* A weight of 1 or more means that the normal number of points are generated nearby.

If nothing is connected, the default weight is 1 for all points. This is an interpreted auto port that accepts the following types:
* A single float uses the same weight for all points.
* An array<float> uses the corresponding array element as the weight for each point. The array may be resized to match the number of points, if necessary.
* A string uses the values of the property with that name as the weights. The property must exist on the geometry and consist of a float value per point.
* A ScalarField uses the field's value at each point's position as the weight.
* An array<long> specifies the indices of the points that have a weight of 1. All other points are considered to have a weight of 0.

### `random_per_point`
When this is checked, the amount, radius and seed are randomized per input point.

## Scatter Settings
### `amount`
The amount of points you wish to scatter per input point.

### `scatter_radius`
The maximum radius from the input point to scatter to.

### `seed`
The seed for the random number generator.

## Profile Settings
The profile settings control the distribution of the scattered points. From center(0) to edge(1).

### `curve`
Use a profile curve to control the distribution.

### `profile_curve`
The profile curve of the distribution.

### `exponential`
Use an exponential distribution.

### `exponent`
The exponent to use for the distribution.  pow(position, exponent).

### `Gauss A`
Use a gaussian distribution based on sine.

### `Gauss B`
Use a gaussian distribution based on cosine.

### `mean`
The expected value of the gaussian distribution.

### `standard_deviation`
The dispersion of the gaussian distribution.

## Display
### `center_color`
The color at the center of the scatter.  This is a lerp from center to edge.

### `edge_color`
The color at the edge of the scatter.  This is a lerp from center to edge.

### `display_shape`
The shape for the viewport display. (Point, Disc, Circle, Quad, Cube, Sphere, Numeric)

### `color_is_profile`
When this is checked, the colour lerp uses the "curve" profile curve

### `color_profile`
The color profile curve controls the colour distribution from center(0) to edge(1).

## Outputs
All outputs are nested arrays by input points.  For example, if you are scattering on 5 points, each output will be a nested array of 5 arrays, each containing the output.

### `points`
The resulting points object.

### `positions`
The float3 vectors of the scattered positions.

### `normals`
The float3 vectors of the scattered normals.

### `colors`
The float3 vectors of the scattered colors.

### `local_center_distances`
The float values of the distance from the point to the local center.

# master loop
This loops through the incoming points (the points to scatter on) and generates points in a sphere around them.  Dive in to see how this works.

# half and half random

A little custom compound that  generates a random value between half of the input value and one-and-a-half times the input value.

# half and half random

A little custom compound that  generates a random value between half of the input value and one-and-a-half times the input value.

## point generation

The points around the input points are generated here

# distribution
Using a curve, exponent or gaussian system will change the distribution of points from 0-1.

For example a curve in a "S-shape" will put more points at the center and at the edge of the sphere.

# construct the points object

in this compound we construct the points from positions and add the *point_color* and *point_size* attributes to the points object.

# points in a sphere
Mathematically calculates  uniform random points inside a sphere.

# uniform spherical distribution

This compound is built using this formula for generating random points in a sphere:

```
https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/87230/picking-random-points-in-the-volume-of-sphere-with-uniform-probability
```

# from_geometry
A polygon sphere, displaced. The point positions are used as the basis points for ***scatter_on_points***
Random position generator - this can be replaced by any positions, for example, the point positions of a mesh. (See the *Dummy Geo* section above.)
